subject: RECORD clause
notes: SR2 is a LEXICAL permission, so it is discharged by the general format admitting both words rather than by a screen: all three formats of 13.18.43.2 print the same { BYTES | CHARACTERS } brace group and recordClause now writes (CHARACTERS | BYTES) in both of its alternatives. Before kb/Work PB721 BYTES had no lexer token at all and `RECORD CONTAINS 20 BYTES` was refused COBOL1970 as an unrecognized file description clause. EDITIONS = 2023 ONLY, derived not assumed: Annex E.3.3 item 13 lists BYTES among the words 'added to the list of context-sensitive words or the context in which they are reserved has been expanded' at 2023, and 8.10 gives BYTES exactly ONE construct - the RECORD clause - so there is no earlier context for that sentence's second arm to name and the spelling did not exist below 2023. VersionConformancePass.VisitRecordClause refuses it at 85/2002/2014 (COBOL0900, constructs.json row record-clause-bytes-2023), the CONTINUE AFTER ... SECONDS precedent from the same item-13 list; the gate is a parse arm rather than a {is2023()}? predicate because the word sits mid-alternative, where a semantic predicate does not steer prediction. ONLY THE CLAUSE IS GATED: CHARACTERS is 1985-continuous, and BYTES stays a nameSlot user word (cobol-words.json), so `01 BYTES PIC X.` and a table and a paragraph named BYTES are legal COBOL-85 - conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb721_bytes_user_word_85 is that over-rejection twin.
